mcqs.learning_point: Relate temperature to molecular kinetic energy
mcqs.question: How is the absolute temperature of an ideal gas related to the average translational kinetic energy of its molecules?

options.A: It is directly proportional to the average translational kinetic energy of the molecules.
options.B: It is inversely proportional to the average translational kinetic energy of the molecules.
options.C: It is independent of the average translational kinetic energy of the molecules.
options.D: It is proportional to the square of the average translational kinetic energy of the molecules.

mcqs.answer: It is directly proportional to the average translational kinetic energy of the molecules.
mcqs.explanation: For an ideal gas, the average translational kinetic energy per molecule is (3/2)k_B T. Hence temperature is directly proportional to the average kinetic energy. Option B is opposite, C ignores the relationship, and D misrepresents the proportionality.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best describes the root‑mean‑square (rms) speed of gas molecules?

options.A: The arithmetic mean of the speeds of all molecules.
options.B: The square root of the average of the squares of the molecular speeds.
options.C: The speed of the most probable molecule in the distribution.
options.D: The minimum speed that any molecule can have.

mcqs.answer: The square root of the average of the squares of the molecular speeds.
mcqs.explanation: rms speed is defined as v_rms = √(⟨v^2⟩), i.e., the square root of the mean of the squared speeds. Option A describes simple average, C describes most probable speed, and D is incorrect because molecules can have very low speeds.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate molecular speed to temperature and molar mass
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly relates the rms speed (v_rms) of a gas to its absolute temperature (T) and molar mass (M)?

options.C: v_rms is directly proportional to the product T·M.
options.D: v_rms is independent of the molar mass of the gas.

mcqs.explanation: From kinetic theory, v_rms = √(3RT/M); thus it varies as the square root of temperature divided by molar mass. Option B inverts the relationship, C suggests linear dependence, and D ignores the mass effect.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate temperature to molecular kinetic energy
mcqs.question: If the absolute temperature of an ideal gas is doubled, what happens to the average translational kinetic energy of its molecules?

options.B: It is reduced to half its original value.

mcqs.explanation: Average translational kinetic energy per molecule is (3/2)k_B T, so it varies linearly with temperature. Doubling T doubles the kinetic energy. Options B and C give incorrect proportionalities, D ignores the temperature dependence.

mcqs.question: Helium gas (molar mass = 4 g mol⁻¹) is at 300 K. Using v_rms = √(3RT/M), what is its rms speed? (R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, convert M to kg mol⁻¹)
mcqs.explanation: M = 4 g mol⁻¹ = 0.004 kg mol⁻¹. v_rms = √[3·8.314·300 / 0.004] ≈ √1.87 × 10⁶ ≈ 1.36 × 10³ m s⁻¹. The other options result from incorrect arithmetic or unit errors.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate molecular speed to temperature and molar mass
mcqs.question: Two gases, hydrogen (M = 2 g mol⁻¹) and nitrogen (M = 28 g mol⁻¹), are kept at the same temperature of 400 K. Which gas has the higher rms speed?

options.C: Both have the same rms speed
options.D: It depends on the pressure of the gases

mcqs.explanation: v_rms ∝ √(T/M). With identical T, the gas with smaller molar mass (hydrogen) has larger √(1/M) and thus higher rms speed. Pressure does not affect rms speed directly, so options C and D are wrong.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate temperature to molecular kinetic energy
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about temperature and kinetic energy is correct?

options.A: Temperature is proportional to the total kinetic energy of all molecules in a sample.
options.B: Temperature is proportional to the average kinetic energy per molecule.
options.C: Temperature depends primarily on the potential energy of intermolecular forces.
options.D: Temperature is unrelated to molecular motion.

mcqs.answer: Temperature is proportional to the average kinetic energy per molecule.
mcqs.explanation: Temperature reflects the average translational kinetic energy per molecule, not the total kinetic energy (which also depends on the number of molecules). Options C and D are false; temperature is a measure of molecular motion, not potential energy.

mcqs.question: If the rms speed of a gas at temperature T is v, what will be its rms speed when the temperature is increased to 4T while the molar mass remains unchanged?

options.A: It becomes twice as large as v.
options.B: It becomes four times as large as v.
options.C: It becomes half as large as v.
options.D: It remains the same as v.

mcqs.answer: It becomes twice as large as v.
mcqs.explanation: Since v_rms ∝ √T, raising T to 4T multiplies the rms speed by √4 = 2. Therefore the speed doubles. Options B, C, and D misapply the square‑root relationship.
